targets.proposed_claim_scope: late first century BCE Hamadab war-captivity testimony; no Kush-wide practice inference
targets.prior_review: data/research/ancient_expansion_03/candidate_review_notes.json: Kush/Meroe deferred; captive iconography alone does not establish enslaved status
targets.source_check: Claude Rilly's REM 1039 reading, as summarized in https://lanfrica.com/en/record/fragments-of-the-meroitic-report-of-the-war-between-rome-and-meroe, describes the Tmey (Romans) enslaving Meroitic men, women, girls and boys. If accepted, its direction is Roman action against Meroites, not proof of Meroitic territorial enslavement practice. REM 1003/EA1650 depicts bound prisoners but does not by itself establish their legal or labour status.
targets.needed: Inspect Rilly's full REM 1039 reading, source-language uncertainty and REM 1003/EA1650 separately. Resolve agent, victim and geography of any enslavement proposition against the prior review before intake.

targets.proposed_claim_scope: 956 and 987 nobi status legislation; legal status and actual practice must be assessed separately
targets.source_check: The Academy of Korean Studies account identifies the 956 emancipation review and 987 re-enslavement rule for some freed nobi; the National Institute of Korean History corroborates those dated laws at https://contents.history.go.kr/front/tg/view.do?ganada=%EC%A0%84%EC%B2%B4&levelId=tg_002_0350&pageUnit=50&treeId=0209. These are discrete legal-status events, not evidence of continuous uniform practice from 956 through 987.
targets.needed: Run exact-head disposable legal-event/research-result idempotency rehearsal. Broader nobi territorial-practice classification and geometry remain HOLD.

targets.proposed_claim_scope: ca. 1715-1850 captive supply and trade; distinct territorial, network and site claims
targets.source_check: Robin Law's 1989 specialist study distinguishes royal raiding, inland purchase and private merchants; it also discusses nineteenth-century palm-oil production using enslaved labour (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-african-history/article/abs/slaveraiders-and-middlemen-monopolists-and-freetraders-the-supply-of-slaves-for-the-atlantic-trade-in-dahomey-c-17151850/25FD3A6506F945524A260237736CA0BB). His 1977 study rejects a blanket royal-monopoly account and distinguishes private merchants from royal control of army captives (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-african-history/article/abs/royal-monopoly-and-private-enterprise-in-the-atlantic-trade-the-case-of-dahomey1/885FB97D2FA6B22C2C762862DD6DB609). Both are one author's related interpretation, not independent corroboration. Publisher abstracts are leads; exact passage/version and claim-level locators remain to be checked.
targets.needed: Run exact-head disposable importer/idempotency rehearsal; historical Jakin/royal-camp geometry stays unresolved and no polity-wide extent is admitted.

targets.proposed_claim_scope: ca. 1450-1521 tlacotin status and terminology require category-specific review
targets.source_check: Camilla Townsend's specialist chapter warns that coerced community labour in Mesoamerican agricultural states should not all be classified as slavery and distinguishes war-captive and domestic enslavement (https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/abs/cambridge-world-history-of-slavery/slavery-in-precontact-america/090D3E244D8E3F465822F387EFED7122). The publisher summary alone does not verify the worker packet's particular tlacotin debt or self-sale assertions. Those propositions need exact category-specific passages and source dependence review.
targets.needed: Keep distinct Nahua categories; accept only after identity/numeric applicability/category review, then run importer replay.
